2015.note: A hot, dry year of great, rich, concentrated crus, Moulin-à-Vent especially. Mature and holding at the top.

2014.note: A fine September rescued the year, giving fresh, classic crus with lovely fruit and good acidity. Mature now; drink up.

2013.note: A cold spring and a late harvest gave fresh, light crus with high acidity. Past its best now.

2012.note: Hail and rot made a tiny, difficult vintage with lean wines. Past its best now.

2011.note: An early, warm year of ripe, generous crus. Drink up now; only top Moulin-à-Vent still has much to give.

2010.note: A small crop of concentrated, structured crus with good acidity. Drink up now; Morgon Côte du Py has held best.

2009.note: A hot, celebrated year of rich, ripe, concentrated crus that sold out quickly. Drink up the remaining bottles.

2008.note: A wet year of light, sometimes dilute Gamay with little to keep it going. Past its best now.

2007.note: A wet summer gave light, early-drinking wines with modest fruit. Past its best now.

2006.note: A good, balanced year of fresh crus for medium-term drinking. Past its best now.

2005.note: A great, structured vintage for the crus, especially Moulin-à-Vent and Morgon. Drink up now from good cellars.

2004.note: A light, rainy year of thin Gamay without much ageing potential. Past its best for every cru.

2003.note: The heatwave made rich, alcoholic, sometimes jammy crus that impressed in youth. Past its best now.

2002.note: A wet harvest and rot made a poor vintage across the region. Past its best now.

2001.note: A wet year of light, lean wines that were best within a few years. Past its best now.

2000.note: A good year of supple, fruity crus for early and medium-term drinking. Past its best now.

1999.note: A good year of ripe, balanced crus with good structure in Moulin-à-Vent. Past its best now.

1998.note: A good year of fresh, balanced crus for medium-term drinking. Past its best now.

1997.note: A ripe, warm year of soft, generous crus that drank early. Past its best now.

1996.note: A fresh, high-acid year of lighter crus that aged reasonably. Past its best now.

1995.note: A good year of ripe, attractive crus for medium-term drinking. Past its best now.

1994.note: A wet year of light, dilute Gamay with little to offer now. Past its best now.

1993.note: A wet year of lean crus with little ageing potential. Past its best now.

1992.note: A light, large crop of easy, short-lived Gamay. Past its best now.

1991.note: A very good year for the crus, ripe and structured, long underrated. Past its best now.

1990.note: A ripe, warm year of rich, generous crus with real depth. Past its best now.

2024.note: A wet spring, hail and mildew, then a generous crop that struggled to build sugar. Expect lighter, lower-alcohol Barolo with bright acidity; selection decided quality. Released from 2028.

2023.note: Spring rain and disease pressure, hail in places and an August heatwave brought an early harvest. Barbaresco from the year is mid-weight with polished tannins; Barolo, released in 2027, looks similar and uneven.

2022.note: A dry winter and a hot, dry summer cut yields by 30 to 40 percent. Open aromatics and fine-grained tannins at best, dilution and alcohol over 15 percent at worst. Serralunga was most consistent; earlier drinking than 2021.

2021.note: A long, even season with cool nights produced classic, perfumed, deeply structured Barolo with bright acidity, widely hailed as exceptional. Built for decades; leave the crus alone.

2020.note: A warm year without extremes gave elegant, aromatic, supple Barolo with ripe tannins and early charm. Very good; the classic bottlings are nearly ready.

2019.note: A cool spring, a warm summer and a long autumn produced fresh, structured, classically proportioned Barolo with high acidity. A great vintage still in its youth.

2018.note: A wet spring and a humid summer brought disease and uneven ripening. Lighter, perfumed, early-drinking Barolo; the best are charming and graceful. Drinking now.

2017.note: Spring frost, then extreme heat and drought. Ripe fruit with firm, sometimes drying tannins; quality is uneven, best in cooler, higher sites. Approachable now.

2016.note: A long, cool, even season gave perfumed, powerful, beautifully balanced Barolo, a modern legend. Still closed; the crus need until the 2030s.

2015.note: A hot summer gave ripe, generous, rounded Barolo with softer acidity. Very good and drinking well now, with the crus holding.

2014.note: A wet summer and hail on parts of La Morra and Barolo made a difficult year; Castiglione Falletto and Serralunga did better. Light, fragrant wines; drink now.

2013.note: A late, cool season and an October harvest gave tense, structured, classic Barolo with superb aromatics. Underrated at release, now emerging.

2012.note: A hot, dry summer after a wet spring gave uneven, ripe Barolo, attractive but less deep than 2013. Drinking well now.

2011.note: A hot, early year of ripe, forward, generous Barolo with soft acidity. Classic bottlings are mature; MGA crus and Riservas are at their peak and hold a few years more.

2010.note: A cool, long season produced great, classic, structured Barolo with depth and freshness. The crus are just opening and will last decades.

2009.note: A hot year of ripe, soft, forward Barolo, sometimes lacking acidity. Mature; drink up over the next few years.

2008.note: A cool, rainy spring and a fine autumn gave fresh, classic, high-acid Barolo with fine tannins. At its peak now.

2007.note: A mild winter and a warm year gave ripe, generous, early-charming Barolo. Mature and drinking well.

2006.note: A warm year that produced powerful, tannic, structured Barolo that needed long ageing. Now opening; great crus have decades left.

2005.note: October rain caught late Nebbiolo and diluted the crop. Good, mid-weight Barolo from careful producers. Mature now.

2004.note: A generous, balanced, classic year with fine tannins and aromatics. Great Barolo at its peak and holding.

2003.note: The heatwave left Nebbiolo stressed, with cooked fruit and hard tannins. Past its best for most wines.

2002.note: Hail in September and persistent rain made a poor year; several leading producers made no Barolo cru. Past.

2001.note: A great, classic, structured vintage of depth and balance. Mature and splendid, with the crus holding.

2000.note: A hot year of ripe, forward, sweet-fruited Barolo, much hyped at release. Mature now; drink up.

1999.note: A classic, firm, structured vintage that needed time and now drinks beautifully. Mature and holding.

1998.note: A good, structured vintage overshadowed by 1997 and 1999. Mature and drinking well.

1997.note: A hot year of opulent, ripe, low-acid Barolo that was hugely praised young and aged unevenly. Drink up now.

1996.note: A cool, late year of great, high-acid, tannic Barolo, a classic for the long haul. Mature now and still vigorous.

1995.note: Hail and an uneven season gave mixed Barolo. Past its best for most wines.

1994.note: Rain in September diluted a promising crop and brought rot to the late-picked Nebbiolo. Light, short-lived Barolo, now past its best.

1993.note: An uneven, rain-affected year with some decent wines. Past its best now.

1992.note: A cold, wet summer and a rainy harvest made one of the poorest Barolo years of the era. Long past its best.

1991.note: A light, uneven vintage after a cool season, overshadowed by 1990. Past its best now.

1990.note: A hot, dry year of great, ripe, powerful Barolo. Mature and splendid.

1989.note: A great, structured vintage, often preferred to 1990 by traditionalists. Mature and still vigorous.

1988.note: A classic, firm, high-acid vintage of good depth that opened slowly, the first of a great trio. Mature and holding at the top.

1985.note: A warm, even year of great, balanced, sweet-fruited Barolo that aged beautifully from traditional cellars. Mature now and lovely.

1982.note: A ripe, rich vintage of good structure, overshadowed by the 1978 and 1985 classics. Mature now; drink up.

1978.note: A small, legendary vintage of power and tannin. Mature now; great bottles are glorious.

1971.note: A legendary vintage, long-lived and perfumed, the benchmark for traditional Barolo of the era. Mature now; provenance decides.

1964.note: A great, classic vintage of balance and longevity, from a time of long macerations and large casks. Mature now; provenance decides.

1961.note: A legendary vintage of rare concentration from a small crop. Mature now; provenance decides everything at this age.

1958.note: A legendary, long-lived vintage from the traditional cellars of Barolo and Serralunga. Mature now; provenance decides everything at this age.

2024.note: A wet, cool season with hail and mildew. Lighter, fresh, lower-alcohol Nebbiolo is expected; selection decided quality. Releases begin in 2027.

2023.note: Wet May and June weather raised disease pressure, hail hit some areas and an August heatwave brought an early harvest. Mid-weight, balanced Barbaresco with riper, more polished tannins than 2022; some dilution from high yields.

2022.note: A dry winter and a scorching summer stressed the vines and cut yields. Open, aromatic, moderately structured Barbaresco at best; some are heavy. Drink earlier than 2021.

2021.note: A long, even season gave classic, perfumed, structured Barbaresco of great purity. Exceptional and long-lived; crus need patience.

2020.note: A warm year without extremes gave elegant, aromatic, supple Barbaresco with ripe tannins. Very good and approachable now.

2019.note: A cool spring and a long autumn gave fresh, classic, structured Barbaresco with high acidity. Very good to excellent; opening now.

2018.note: A wet, humid season brought disease and uneven ripening. Light, perfumed Barbaresco for early drinking. Drink now.

2017.note: Frost, heat and drought gave ripe fruit and firm tannins; uneven. Drink now.

2016.note: A long, cool season gave perfumed, powerful, balanced Barbaresco, a modern great. Opening now; the crus need more time.

2015.note: A hot summer gave ripe, generous, rounded Barbaresco with softer acidity. Drinking well now and holding at the crus.

2014.note: A wet summer, but Barbaresco escaped the worst of the hail and made fragrant, balanced wines, more successful than Barolo. At their peak.

2013.note: A late, cool season gave tense, classic Barbaresco with fine aromatics. Very good and drinking well.

2012.note: A hot summer after a wet spring gave ripe, uneven wines. Mature now.

2011.note: A hot, early year with an August heatwave gave ripe, forward, generous Barbaresco with soft acidity. Classic bottlings are mature now; MGA crus from traditional cellars are at their peak.

2010.note: A cool, long season gave great, classic Barbaresco. At its peak with years to go.

2009.note: A hot year of ripe, soft, forward wines lacking a little acidity. Mature; drink up.

2008.note: A cool year of fresh, classic, high-acid Barbaresco with fine tannins. Mature and drinking well.

2007.note: A mild winter and a warm, early year gave ripe, generous, open Barbaresco with soft tannins. Mature now and drinking well.

2006.note: A warm year of structured, tannic Barbaresco that needed time to unwind. Mature and holding at the top crus.

2005.note: Harvest rain diluted the crop and lightened the wines. Past its best for most bottlings.

2004.note: A generous, balanced, classic year with fine tannins and lifted aromatics, a great Barbaresco vintage. At its peak now.

2003.note: The heatwave left Nebbiolo stressed, with cooked fruit and hard tannins. Past its best now.

2002.note: September hail and persistent rain made a poor vintage; several leading producers declassified. Past its best.

2001.note: A great, classic, structured vintage with deep fruit and fine acidity. Mature and splendid now.

2000.note: A hot year of ripe, forward, sweet-fruited wines much praised at release. Drink up now.

1999.note: A classic, firm, structured vintage that needed time and now drinks beautifully. Mature now.

1998.note: A good, structured vintage overshadowed by 1997 and 1999 but often more balanced. Mature now.

1997.note: A hot year of opulent, ripe, low-acid wines that aged unevenly. Drink up now.

1996.note: A cool, late year of great, high-acid, tannic Barbaresco built for the long haul. Mature and still vigorous at the top.

1995.note: Hail and an uneven season gave mixed Barbaresco with some fine single-vineyard wines. Past its best now.

1994.note: September rain diluted the crop and brought rot. Light Barbaresco, long past its best.

1993.note: An uneven, rain-affected year with some decent wines from careful producers. Past its best now.

1992.note: A cold, wet summer and a rainy harvest made a poor vintage. Long past its best.

1991.note: A light, uneven vintage after a cool season. Past its best now.

1990.note: A hot, dry year of great, ripe, powerful Barbaresco. Mature now; drink up the classic bottlings.

1989.note: A great, structured vintage often preferred to 1990 by traditionalists. Mature and holding at the top crus.

1985.note: A warm, even year of great, balanced Barbaresco that aged gracefully. Mature now and lovely.

1978.note: A small, legendary vintage of power and tannin. Mature now; provenance decides everything at this age.

1971.note: A legendary, perfumed and long-lived vintage. Mature now; provenance decides everything at this age.

2024.note: Record spring rain in central Italy brought mildew, then a hot, dry summer. Quality depends on the estate's disease control; expect ripe, mid-weight Brunello. Released in 2029.

2023.note: Downy mildew devastated parts of central Italy after a wet May and June, then August heat followed. Small volumes of ripe Sangiovese; uneven. Released in 2028.

2022.note: A hot, dry summer was eased by August rain. Ripe, deep, balanced Sangiovese with firm tannins from the better-exposed slopes. Released in 2027.

2021.note: April frost, then a dry, even summer with cool nights. Intense, perfumed, deeply structured Brunello with vibrant acidity, received as an outstanding vintage on release in 2026. Hold.

2020.note: A warm year with a well-timed late-summer rain gave elegant, aromatic, supple Brunello that is approachable on release. Very good.

2019.note: An even season with cool nights produced classic, balanced, fresh and powerful Brunello. A great vintage that needs time.

2018.note: A rainy spring and a humid summer brought disease pressure. Lighter, elegant, perfumed Brunello for earlier drinking; very good from careful estates.

2017.note: Spring frost and an extreme summer drought gave ripe, dense, sometimes hard Brunello. Uneven; the higher, cooler sites did best.

2016.note: A cool, long, even season gave perfumed, fresh, structured Brunello of great depth, one of the finest modern vintages. Opening now.

2015.note: A hot summer gave ripe, rich, generous Brunello with plush tannins. Excellent and drinking well now.

2014.note: A wet, cool summer brought disease and dilution; many estates declassified into Rosso. Light Brunello; drink now.

2013.note: A cool, late year of classic, fresh, aromatic Brunello with firm structure. Very good and at its peak.

2012.note: A hot, dry summer gave dense, ripe Brunello with good tannins and dark fruit. Very good and drinking well now.

2011.note: An August heatwave gave ripe, forward, generous Brunello with soft acidity. Mature now; enjoy rather than keep.

2010.note: A cool, even season gave great, classic, balanced Brunello with deep fruit and fine acidity. At its peak with decades to go.

2009.note: A warm year of ripe, forward, sweet-fruited Brunello with modest structure. Mature now; drink up.

2008.note: A cool, rainy year with uneven Brunello; the best are fresh, classic and fine-boned. Mature now.

2003.note: The heatwave gave baked, tannic Brunello with low acidity and dry tannins. Past its best now.

2002.note: Persistent rain made a poor vintage and many estates released no Brunello at all. Past its best.

2022.note: A hot, dry summer eased by August rain. Ripe, balanced Sangiovese with good acidity; very good Riserva and Gran Selezione.

2020.note: A warm year with fresh, elegant, aromatic Sangiovese. Very good; drinking well.

2019.note: An even year of classic, balanced, perfumed wines. Excellent Riserva and Gran Selezione at an early peak.

2018.note: A rainy spring and a humid summer gave lighter, elegant, perfumed Sangiovese. Drink now; Riservas are at their peak.

2017.note: Frost and drought gave a small crop of ripe, firm wines. Drink now.

2016.note: A cool, long season gave great, fresh, structured Chianti Classico. At its peak.

2015.note: A hot, dry year of ripe, generous, rich Sangiovese with plush tannins. Riservas are at their peak.

2014.note: A wet, cool summer brought disease and dilution. Light wines, many declassified to annata. Drink up now.

2013.note: A cool, late year of classic, fresh, aromatic Sangiovese with firm structure. Mature and drinking well.

2012.note: A hot, dry, uneven year of ripe, sometimes rustic Sangiovese. Mature now; drink up the Riservas.

2011.note: An August heatwave gave forward, generous wines with soft acidity. Drink up now.

2010.note: A cool, classic year of fresh, perfumed, firm Sangiovese. Mature and drinking well.

2009.note: A warm year of soft, round wines for medium-term drinking. Past its best for most Riservas.

2008.note: A cool, uneven year with some fresh, classic Riservas. Past its best for most.

2007.note: A warm, even year of ripe, generous, well-balanced wines. Drink up now.

2006.note: A great, structured year of deep, long-lived Riservas with firm tannins. Mature and holding.

2005.note: Rain at harvest diluted the crop and Riservas were few. Past its best now.

2004.note: A classic, balanced, even year with fine Riservas. Drink up now; few will improve.

2003.note: The heatwave gave baked, tannic, low-acid Sangiovese that lost its charm early. Past its best now.

2002.note: Persistent rain made a very poor year; many estates made no Riserva. Long past its best.

2001.note: A classic, balanced year after spring frost, with firm Riservas. Past its best for most bottles now.

2000.note: A hot year of soft, early-maturing wines with modest acidity. Past its best now.

1999.note: A very good, balanced year of ripe, structured wines. Past its best now for most.

1998.note: A good year of medium weight overshadowed by 1997 and 1999. Past its best now.

1997.note: A great, ripe, generous year that put Tuscany in the spotlight. Past its best for most Riservas now.

1996.note: An uneven, rain-affected year of lighter, leaner wines. Past its best now.

1995.note: A very good, firm year with good Riservas. Past its best now.

2023.note: Hail in summer and heat at harvest reduced healthy fruit for appassimento. Expect ripe, uneven Amarone.

2022.note: A hot, dry year gave small, thick-skinned, healthy berries that dried well. Concentrated, ripe Amarone.

2021.note: An even season with cool nights gave healthy, aromatic grapes for drying. Balanced, fresh, very good Amarone.

2020.note: A warm year with some harvest rain gave good, mid-weight Amarone that drinks early. Approachable now.

2019.note: A cool spring and a warm summer gave fresh, aromatic, balanced Amarone. Very good.

2018.note: A large crop and a humid season gave softer, earlier-drinking Amarone with less concentration than usual.

2017.note: Frost and drought cut yields and concentrated the grapes. Dense, powerful Amarone.

2016.note: An even season and healthy grapes gave great, balanced, fresh Amarone with fine acidity. Built for the long term.

2015.note: A hot, dry year of rich, concentrated, great Amarone with healthy grapes for drying. Drinking well now and long-lived.

2014.note: A cold, wet summer left little healthy fruit for drying; many estates made no Amarone.

2013.note: A late, cool year of fresh, classic, balanced Amarone with lively acidity. Mature and drinking well.

2012.note: A hot summer gave ripe, generous grapes that dried well into rich, supple Amarone. Very good and drinking well.

2011.note: A warm year and healthy grapes made a great, powerful vintage of rich, balanced Amarone. At its peak.

2010.note: A cool year of fresh, elegant, perfumed Amarone with lively acidity. Mature and drinking well.

2008.note: A classic, balanced vintage of good freshness and depth, drying in good autumn conditions. Mature now.

2007.note: A warm, early vintage of ripe, softer Amarone. Mature now; drink up.

2006.note: A great vintage of healthy grapes and rich, balanced, long-lived Amarone. Mature and holding.

2005.note: A wet harvest limited the fruit fit for drying. Light Amarone; past its best now.

2004.note: A good, balanced vintage of medium weight with healthy drying grapes. Mature now.

2002.note: A wet, poor year with little healthy fruit for drying; little Amarone was made. Past its best.

2001.note: A classic, balanced vintage of good depth and freshness. Mature now; drink over the next few years.

2000.note: A rich, ripe vintage of generous, powerful Amarone with high alcohol. Mature now; drink up.

1999.note: A good vintage of medium weight and freshness. Past its best for most bottles now.

1997.note: A great, ripe, concentrated vintage, one of the finest of the decade. Mature now.

2022.note: A warm year with welcome rain gave balanced, aromatic Nerello Mascalese with fine tannins. Very good.

2015.note: A hot year of ripe, generous, rich wines. Very good and drinking well.

2014.note: Rain at harvest made an uneven year with lighter, fresher wines. Good; drink now.

2013.note: A cool, late, rainy year of lean, high-acid Tempranillo. Drink up.

2012.note: A dry year with a small crop of concentrated wines. Very good.

2011.note: A hot year of ripe, powerful, dark-fruited wines with firm tannins. Very good and mature.

2010.note: A great, classic, balanced vintage of fresh, structured Tempranillo. At its peak now.

2009.note: A great, ripe, concentrated vintage of dense, generous wines. At its peak now.

2008.note: A cool, late year of fresh, lighter wines with high acidity. Mature now.

2007.note: A cool year of lighter, fresh wines. Drink up the remaining Reservas.

2006.note: A very good, balanced year of ripe, supple wines. Mature now.

2005.note: A great, structured vintage of concentrated, long-lived wines. Mature and holding.

2004.note: A great, classic vintage of balance and depth from a long season. Mature and holding.

2003.note: A hot year of ripe, soft wines with low acidity. Past their best now.

2002.note: A cool, wet year of lean wines. Past its best now.

2001.note: A great vintage of concentrated, structured wines, rated among the best of its decade. Mature now.

2000.note: A large crop of good, supple wines. Past their best now.

1999.note: A very good vintage of firm, concentrated wines. Past its best for most bottles.

1998.note: A good vintage of medium weight. Past its best now.

1997.note: A wet year of light, dilute wines. Long past its best.

1996.note: A great vintage of rich, structured wines, the first of a celebrated pair. Drink up now.

1995.note: A great, concentrated vintage that helped build Ribera's modern reputation. Drink up now.

1994.note: A very good vintage of firm, deep wines. Past its best for most bottles.

1993.note: A wet year of light wines. Long past its best.

1992.note: A good vintage of medium weight. Past its best now.

1991.note: A very good vintage of firm, concentrated wines. Past its best now.

1990.note: A very good vintage of ripe, structured wines. Past its best now.

2022.note: A hot, dry year of ripe, powerful wines; the cooler, higher sites did best. Good.

2021.note: A balanced year of fresh, vibrant, mineral wines with fine tannins from the slate. Very good.

2020.note: Mildew cut yields in a wet spring, then a warm summer concentrated the rest. Very good.

2019.note: A warm, dry year of ripe, concentrated, balanced wines with good freshness. Very good.

2018.note: A cooler, wetter year of fresh, elegant, classic Priorat with fine tannins. Excellent.

2017.note: A hot, dry year with a small crop of ripe, dense wines. Good; drinking now.

2016.note: A balanced year of very good, fresh, mineral wines. At its peak now.

2015.note: A great, ripe, structured vintage with depth and freshness. At its peak now.

2014.note: A fresh, balanced year of vibrant Garnacha and Cariñena. Very good and drinking well.

2013.note: A cool year of elegant, fresh, mineral wines. Very good and mature now.

2012.note: A dry year with a small crop of concentrated wines. Very good.

2011.note: A warm year of ripe, generous wines with soft acidity. Very good and mature.

2004.note: A great vintage of balance and freshness from a long season. Mature now.

2002.note: A wet year of lighter wines. Past its best now.

2000.note: A very good vintage of ripe, powerful wines. Past its best now.

1995.note: A great vintage from the first decade of the modern Priorat estates. Drink up now.

2023.note: A welcomingly wet, temperate year after several hot ones. Quinta do Noval made the only full classic declaration; Symington released single-quinta wines and Taylor's its Sentinels blend.

2022.note: July was the hottest in Portugal since 1931 and heatwaves were long. Selective releases: Taylor's launched its first Sentinels blend, Symington made single-quinta wines.

2021.note: A cooler year spoilt by September rain. No general declaration: Noval declared, Symington released single-quinta wines, and the Fladgate houses made none. Windows refer to single-quinta wines.

2020.note: A hot, early year in which Touriga Nacional coped best. Single-quinta wines rather than classic declarations from the major houses.

2019.note: A dry year with moderate temperatures in summer gave balanced wines released mostly as single-quinta Vintage Ports.

2018.note: A cold, wet spring with hail, then a hot summer brought the grapes round. Mostly single-quinta wines from the major houses.

2017.note: Drought and heat gave the earliest harvest since 1945 and tiny, concentrated berries. Widely declared, the second classic year in a row and Symington's last general declaration before 2024.

2016.note: A cold, wet spring cut the crop, then a hot summer and autumn brought full ripeness. Widely declared by the major houses; structured and long-lived.

2015.note: A hot, dry year with an early harvest. Declared by Quinta do Noval and a number of other houses, while the largest groups made no classic declaration and saved themselves for 2016 and 2017.

2014.note: A wet winter and a warm summer, then rain at harvest. Single-quinta wines from the major houses.

2013.note: A cool spring, a dry summer and heavy rain at the end of September. A few single-quinta wines.

2012.note: A dry winter and rain at flowering, then a short heatwave. Single-quinta wines from the major houses.

2011.note: Perfect conditions through ripening and harvest produced a legendary, widely declared vintage that many houses rank with their greatest. Approachable now for the first time.

2010.note: A wet winter refilled reserves for a hot summer; phenolic ripeness came late. Single-quinta wines.

2009.note: Drought reduced yields and concentrated the grapes. A partial declaration led by the Fladgate houses (Taylor's, Fonseca, Croft) and Quinta do Noval rather than a general one.

2008.note: A wet spring with mildew pressure, then a fine finish. Single-quinta wines; some very good.

2007.note: Winter rain refilled reserves and a mild summer gave balanced, aromatic wines. Widely declared.

2006.note: A hot, dry year with June hail that cut yields by up to a third in places. A few single-quinta wines.

2005.note: A very dry year of healthy, concentrated grapes, rated highly by some charts. Released mainly as single-quinta wines from the major houses.

2004.note: A challenging, uneven season rescued by a fine finish. Single-quinta wines from the major houses.

2003.note: The European heatwave, tempered by timely rain, gave rich, ripe, widely declared Vintage Port. Approachable earlier than most classic years.

2002.note: A promising small crop was hit by rain from 13 September. Few wines.

2001.note: A good Port year but not a Vintage Port year for the majors. Single-quinta wines.

2000.note: A small crop after a cool, wet spring gave concentrated, balanced wines; widely declared. At its peak now.

1999.note: Not a Vintage Port year: only a few single-quinta wines were released.

1998.note: A cold, wet spring and a hot summer, then rain. Single-quinta wines.

1997.note: A late, very successful harvest; almost every house declared. Less concentrated than 1994 but elegant.

1996.note: A wet winter and vigorous growth gave a large crop. Single-quinta wines.

1995.note: Relentless August heat shrivelled many grapes, and only a few houses chose to declare.

1994.note: Harvested in fine conditions at the end of September; most houses declared. A great, concentrated, long-lived vintage now opening.

1993.note: Rain and rot ruined the harvest; there is no Vintage Port of note.

1992.note: A handful of houses that had skipped 1991, led by Taylor's and Fonseca, declared 1992.

1991.note: A hot, dry summer and a September harvest; Symington and many others declared.

1990.note: Extreme heat in July and August; only a few houses released Vintage Port.

1985.note: A widely declared vintage of balanced, approachable wines that aged well. Mature now.

1983.note: A firm, tannic, widely declared vintage, slow to open. Mature now.

1980.note: A lighter declared vintage, long undervalued. Mature now; drink up.

1977.note: A great, widely declared vintage, Taylor's and Fonseca especially. Mature and splendid.

1970.note: A great, balanced, widely declared vintage. Mature and splendid now.

1966.note: A classic, elegant declared vintage. Mature now.

1963.note: A legendary vintage, among the greatest of the century. Mature and splendid.

1955.note: A great, widely declared vintage. Mature now.

1948.note: A great vintage from a hot year, declared by fewer houses. Mature now; provenance decides.

1945.note: A legendary, concentrated vintage after a small crop. Mature now; provenance decides.

1931.note: A legendary year, above all for Quinta do Noval Nacional. Mature now; provenance decides.

1927.note: A legendary, widely declared vintage of the inter-war years. Mature now; provenance decides.

2011.note: Blandy's released Malmsey, Verdelho, Sercial and Bual colheitas from 2011 in 2024, praised as textbook young Madeira. Ready on release; decades of life after bottling.

1989.note: Blandy's Sercial and Cossart Gordon Bual frasqueiras from 1989, released in 2024, show intense acidity and savoury depth. Ready now; Madeira of this age is effectively indestructible.

1987.note: Blandy's 1987 Terrantez, released in 2024, was hailed as a thrilling wine. Terrantez is rare and prized for its bittersweet balance. Ready now and for generations.

1981.note: Barbeito's 1981 is still admired by enthusiasts. Vintage Madeira of this age is ready whenever it is opened and lasts long after bottling.

1977.note: Blandy's 1977 Verdelho is described as smoky, refreshing and deep. Ready now; heat and oxygen in cask have already done the ageing.

1975.note: Blandy's 1975 Terrantez shows clove, spice and a long finish. Ready now and for decades.

1935.note: A powerful, long Boal from the HM Borges cellar, with ginger cake and molasses notes. Ready now; bottles in good condition keep indefinitely.

1920.note: Blandy's 1920 Bual is still offered by merchants a century on. Ready now; old Madeira is the most durable wine there is.

1875.note: One of two nineteenth-century harvests remembered as excellent on the island, when every house made Madeira; D'Oliveiras Malvasia 1875 is singled out.

1863.note: Remembered with 1875 as one of the island's two excellent nineteenth-century harvests, made just after the oidium crisis and before phylloxera.

1846.note: HM Borges Terrantez 1846 has been called the best wine its taster ever drank: floral, spicy and fiery. A pre-oidium, pre-phylloxera relic.

2024.note: An April frost and a cool, wet season gave the smallest Mosel crop in fifty years; the Saar and Ruwer lost up to half. Careful selection produced lively, pure, often exciting Riesling in tiny volumes.

2023.note: A warm summer then a wet, humid harvest brought rot and botrytis. Uneven: fine Auslese and some lovely Kabinett from early or careful pickers, softer wines elsewhere.

2022.note: A hot, dry summer rescued by September rain gave ripe, juicy, fruity Riesling with moderate acidity. Charming and early drinking; dry wines are generous.

2021.note: A cool, rainy year and a late October harvest gave high-acid, low-alcohol, electric Riesling, a classic Kabinett and Spätlese vintage of great purity. Built to age.

2020.note: A warm, dry year with an early harvest gave ripe, balanced, aromatic Riesling with good acidity. Very good across the styles.

2019.note: Frost, sunburn and drought reduced yields, and the remaining fruit was concentrated and vibrant with fine acidity. A great all-round year.

2018.note: A hot, dry summer and a big, healthy crop gave ripe, generous, lower-acid Riesling. Very good; enjoy the Kabinetts now.

2017.note: April frost and summer hail cut the crop; what remained was intense and concentrated, with botrytis for sweet wines. Very good.

2016.note: A wet spring with mildew, then a fine autumn gave elegant, balanced, pure Riesling with moderate alcohol. Very good.

2015.note: A hot, dry year that kept freshness gave great, ripe, pure, concentrated Riesling across all styles. At an early peak.

2014.note: Fruit flies and rot forced an early, hurried harvest. Lighter, fresh wines; the best estates sorted well. Drink now.

2013.note: A cold, late season with rot gave high-acid Riesling and some botrytis wines. Good from top estates.

2012.note: A small crop of balanced, elegant, classic Riesling. Very good and at its peak.

2011.note: A warm year with early, clean botrytis gave rich Auslese and beyond; dry and Kabinett wines are softer. Very good.

2010.note: A tiny crop with record acidity, often deacidified, gave piercing, long-lived Riesling. Very good at the top; still taut.

2009.note: A warm year of ripe, generous Riesling with botrytis for sweet wines. Very good and drinking well.

2008.note: A cool, late year of classic, racy Riesling. Very good and mature.

2007.note: A long, mild season gave great, balanced, ripe and racy Riesling. At its peak.

2006.note: A warm summer and rot at harvest; much was botrytised. Uneven; sweet wines can be fine.

2005.note: A great, concentrated vintage with botrytis and high extract. At its peak.

2004.note: A late, cool year of classic, racy Riesling with good acidity and moderate ripeness. Spätlese is mature now and drinking well.

2003.note: The heatwave gave rich, low-acid Riesling; great sweet wines, softer Spätlese. Mature.

2002.note: A classic, fresh, balanced year of elegant Riesling with bright acidity. Mature now; Spätlese has reached its plateau.

2001.note: A great, classic year of ripe, racy, long-lived Riesling. Mature and splendid.

2000.note: Rain and rot spoiled much of the harvest and forced hurried picking. Past its best for most Spätlese.

1999.note: A large, ripe crop of charming, early-maturing Riesling. Mature now; drink the Spätlese.

1998.note: A year of fine Spätlese and great Eiswein after a hard November frost. Mature now, the sweet wines holding best.

1997.note: A ripe, balanced year with clean fruit and moderate acidity. Mature now and best drunk over the next few years.

1996.note: A cool, high-acid, long-lived year whose wines were austere in youth and opened slowly. Mature now.

1995.note: A late year with botrytis gave good sweet wines and fine Spätlese. Mature now.

1994.note: A wet autumn spread botrytis widely and gave fine Auslese and sweet wines. Mature now.

1993.note: A small crop of concentrated Riesling with good acidity. Mature now and holding at the top estates.

1992.note: A large, soft crop of easy, early-drinking Riesling. Past its best for Spätlese.

1991.note: A frosty spring and a cool year of lean, high-acid wines. Past its best now.

1990.note: A great, concentrated, balanced vintage, the finest of its decade along the Mosel. Mature and splendid, with Auslese still youthful.

1989.note: A ripe, warm year with botrytis for fine sweet wines. Mature now; drink the Spätlese.

1988.note: A classic, racy, elegant year with fine acidity. Mature now.

1983.note: A ripe, good year with plenty of Spätlese and Auslese. Mature now; drink up.

1976.note: A hot year of great Auslese, Beerenauslese and Trockenbeerenauslese. Mature now and still lovely from good cellars.

1975.note: A classic, balanced year of elegant Riesling. Mature now; drink up.

1971.note: A legendary year of perfectly balanced Riesling across the Prädikat range. Mature and still thrilling from top estates.

1959.note: A hot year of great, rich sweet wines. Mature; provenance decides now.

1949.note: A great vintage of the post-war years. Mature; provenance decides now.

1921.note: A legendary hot year for sweet Riesling, with famous Trockenbeerenauslesen. Mature; provenance decides now.

2024.note: Frost hit the Rhine-side vineyards and a rainy summer brought downy mildew that cut Rheingau yields more than the frost. The Nahe was patchier. Close selection gave elegant, cool-style Riesling with lively acidity.

2023.note: A warm summer and a wet September brought rot pressure; quick, selective picking was essential. Ripe, open Riesling; uneven.

2022.note: A hot, dry summer eased by September rain gave ripe, generous Riesling with moderate acidity. Good, early-drinking GGs.

2021.note: A cool, wet year with a late harvest gave racy, high-acid, classic Riesling. Very good; GGs need time.

2020.note: A warm, dry year of ripe, balanced, aromatic Riesling with good acidity. Very good; GGs are opening now.

2019.note: A small crop of concentrated, vibrant, balanced Riesling. Excellent; GGs are at an early peak.

2018.note: A hot year with a big crop of ripe, lower-acid Riesling. Very good; drink earlier.

2017.note: Frost and hail cut yields, giving intense, concentrated, structured wines. Very good and drinking well.

2016.note: A wet spring with mildew, then a fine autumn. Elegant, balanced Riesling.

2015.note: A hot, dry, great year of ripe, pure Riesling. At its peak.

2014.note: Rot and fruit flies forced early picking and close sorting. Lighter wines; drink now.

2013.note: A cool, late year of high-acid, firm Riesling. Good; mature now.

2012.note: A small, classic crop of balanced, elegant Riesling. Very good and mature now.

2011.note: A warm, ripe year of generous Riesling with softer acidity. Very good; mature now.

2010.note: A tiny crop with very high acidity gave taut, long-lived Riesling. Very good and still lively.

2009.note: A ripe, generous year of rounded Riesling. Mature now; drink up the GGs.

2008.note: A cool, classic year of racy, high-acid Riesling. Mature now.

2007.note: A long, mild, great year of balanced, ripe and racy Riesling. Mature now.

2006.note: A warm year with rot at harvest gave uneven, botrytis-touched wines. Drink up now.

2005.note: A great, concentrated year of rich, structured Riesling. Mature now.

1995.note: A late year with botrytis. Past its best for dry wines.

1994.note: A botrytis year with fine sweet wines. Past its best for dry wines.

1993.note: A small, concentrated crop. Past its best for dry wines.

1992.note: A large, soft crop. Past its best now.

1991.note: A lean, cool year. Past its best now.

1990.note: A great, concentrated, balanced vintage. Mature now; sweet wines still splendid.

1976.note: A hot year of great Auslese and beyond. Mature now.

1971.note: A legendary, perfectly balanced vintage across the Prädikat range. Mature now.

1959.note: A hot year of great, rich sweet wines. Mature; provenance decides.

1921.note: A legendary hot year with famous sweet Rieslings. Mature; provenance decides.

2024.note: A mild spring brought early budding, then mid-April frost damaged many buds and cut volumes. A warm summer followed; fresh, balanced wines in smaller quantities.

2023.note: A drawn-out harvest that ran into November in the western Wachau gave ripe, balanced Smaragd with good acidity. Very good.

2022.note: Late budding avoided frost; a warm, wet May kept growers busy. Balanced, aromatic, very good wines.

2021.note: A cool, wet spring delayed flowering, limiting frost damage; a fine late summer and autumn gave racy, concentrated, classic Smaragd. Outstanding.

2020.note: Spring frost and August hail damaged parts of the valley. Fresh, uneven wines; the best are elegant.

2019.note: A warm year with high acidity and concentration; excellent Riesling and Grüner Veltliner Smaragd.

2018.note: The earliest harvest on record and a big, healthy crop of very good, ripe wines.

2017.note: A warm year with a crop about a quarter larger than average gave ripe, generous wines. Mature now; drink the Smaragd.

2016.note: Late April frost cut yields, then a fine summer; balanced, fresh wines.

2015.note: A warm, even year of full, ripe wines with typical varietal character. Very good and drinking well now.

2014.note: Persistent rain and grey rot hit Riesling hardest. Only the most selective estates made good Smaragd.

2013.note: Snow, drought and floods made a dramatic year, yet Grüner Veltliner was concentrated and Riesling racy. Very good and mature.

2012.note: May frost reduced the crop; otherwise a good year, full Grüner and fresh Riesling.

2011.note: A warm year of big, rich, higher-alcohol wines with softer acidity. Mature now; drink up.

2010.note: A cold, wet, difficult year with a much smaller crop; Kremstal did best.

2009.note: A small crop of good, ageworthy Riesling and Grüner Veltliner. Mature now.

2008.note: A cool year of racy, high-acid wines that aged slowly. Mature now.

2007.note: A balanced, good vintage of fresh, elegant Smaragd. Mature now; drink up.

2006.note: A warm, healthy year of ripe, great Smaragd with depth. Mature now and still lovely.

2005.note: A wet harvest with rot made an uneven year. Past its best for most.

2004.note: A late, cool year of fresh, lighter wines. Past its best now.

2003.note: Heatwave wines, rich and low in acidity. Past its best now.

2002.note: August floods along the Danube, then a fine autumn and good wines.

2001.note: A classic, balanced year of fine Riesling and Grüner. Past its best for most Smaragd.

2000.note: A warm, early year of ripe wines. Past its best now.

1999.note: A great, concentrated vintage of rich, balanced Smaragd. Drink up now from good cellars.

1998.note: A rich year with some botrytis. Past its best now.

1997.note: A great, balanced vintage of ripe, firm Smaragd. Past its best for most now.

1996.note: A cold, wet, difficult year with lean wines. Long past its best.

1995.note: A good vintage of fresh, balanced wines. Past its best now.

1994.note: A good vintage of ripe wines. Past its best now.

1993.note: A very good vintage of concentrated wines. Past its best now.

1992.note: A warm, rich vintage. Past its best now.

1991.note: A good vintage of fresh wines. Past its best now.

1990.note: A great vintage of concentrated, long-lived Smaragd. Past its best for most bottles now.

2023.note: Described by Disznókő's director as definitely a great vintage, with good dry wines too. Aszú will appear from about 2027.

2022.note: An extremely hot, dry year that held back botrytis; few Aszú wines.

2021.note: A five-star vintage of fresh, citrusy, long-lived Aszú, compared by many to 1999. Worth the wait.

2020.note: A rainy year that was not outstanding for Aszú; dry Furmint fared better. Approachable now.

2019.note: A harmonious year with balanced flavours, neither too sweet nor too acidic.

2018.note: A warm year in which little Aszú was made, as botrytis was patchy. Approachable now.

2017.note: An absolute top vintage; the wines are young but built to live for many decades.

2016.note: Rain required careful berry selection, but the wines are high in acidity, balanced and long-lived.

2015.note: A warm year with few aszú berries; dry and late-harvest wines dominated. Drinking well now.

2014.note: A rainy year with almost no high-quality Aszú; most houses made none. Drink any that exist.

2013.note: An exceptional vintage with abundant aszú berries; the wines have somewhat subdued acidity and sugar.

2012.note: An extremely hot year in which few Aszú wines were made. Drinking well now.

2011.note: An extremely hot year with fewer Aszú wines than usual. Drinking well now.

2010.note: A rainy year that required very careful selection; lower slopes sometimes surprise.

2009.note: Very little Aszú was produced after an uneven botrytis season. Drinking well now.

2008.note: Very good acidity and intense botrytis character; a favourite of insiders. At its peak with decades left.

2007.note: A hot year of broader, richer Aszú that kept plenty of acidity.

2006.note: A harmonious year with a good balance between acidity and sugar. At its peak now.

2005.note: A cooler, moderately good year with fewer Aszú wines. Drinking well now.

2004.note: A cooler, moderately good year with modest botrytis. Drinking well now.

2003.note: A very hot five-star year of rich, powerful Aszú. At its peak with decades left.

2002.note: An inconsistent year that can still surprise from careful houses. Drinking well now.

2000.note: A very hot five-star year whose Aszú is still showing surprisingly well.

1999.note: The benchmark modern vintage, ranked among the greatest of the last millennium.

1993.note: The first great vintage of the post-communist revival, when the new private houses made their names.

2024.note: A warm season punctuated by a July heatwave brought an early harvest of ripe, concentrated Cabernet. Very good, with plusher tannins than 2023; growers who kept canopies intact made the best wines.

2023.note: A wet winter, a cool summer and the longest hang time in years produced fresh, balanced, deeply structured Cabernet with modest alcohol. Hailed as a vintage of a lifetime.

2022.note: Drought and a record Labor Day heatwave in early September split the vintage: fruit picked before the heat is excellent, later picks can be jammy. Very good overall.

2021.note: A second drought year gave small berries and low yields of intense, concentrated, structured Cabernet with fine freshness. Excellent and long-lived.

2020.note: The Glass and LNU Complex fires blanketed the valley in smoke; many leading estates made no Cabernet at all. Wines that were released are lighter; drink them.

2019.note: A wet spring and a moderate summer with a long autumn gave polished, balanced, aromatic Cabernet. Excellent; opening now.

2018.note: A long, cool, even season and a generous crop produced elegant, fresh, beautifully balanced Cabernet. Excellent and now opening.

2017.note: Labor Day heat spikes stressed the vines, and October fires struck after most Cabernet was picked. Uneven but often very good; drinking now.

2016.note: An even, warm season without extremes gave balanced, classic, structured Cabernet. Excellent; at an early peak.

2015.note: The fourth drought year and poor flowering gave a tiny crop of concentrated, tannic Cabernet. Very good; drinking now.

2014.note: Drought and an early harvest, interrupted by the August earthquake that damaged cellars in south Napa. Ripe, approachable, very good wines.

2013.note: An ideal, dry, even season gave dark, structured, powerful Cabernet. Excellent; at the start of its peak.

2012.note: A generous crop in a near-perfect season gave balanced, plush, appealing Cabernet. Very good and drinking well.

2011.note: A cold, wet year with rot at harvest gave lighter, leaner Cabernet. Drink now.

2010.note: A cool summer and sudden late-August heat that sunburned some fruit. Fresh, structured wines from careful growers.

2009.note: A warm year with an October storm; most Cabernet was picked before. Ripe, balanced, very good.

2008.note: Spring frost and heat spikes cut yields. Ripe, concentrated but uneven wines.

2007.note: A small, even, warm year of opulent, rich, great Cabernet. At its peak now.

2006.note: A wet spring and a cool, late year of firm, structured wines. Mature now.

2005.note: A long, cool season and a large crop of balanced, elegant wines. At its peak.

2004.note: An early, warm year with heat spikes gave ripe, forward Cabernet with soft tannins. Mature now; drink over the next few years.

2003.note: A cool spring and late heat made an uneven year; the best mountain Cabernets have aged well. Mature now.
